verdicts.question: What type of roof is present at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 7, 8 and 11: flat cement-finished concrete terrace with concrete parapet walls and a concrete headroom/staircase block; no tiles or sheeting on the main terrace (only a small red-tiled sloped canopy over the stair opening).
verdicts.rationale: RCC flat terrace clearly visible in Staircase Details, Material Storage and PV proposed-area photos.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstructions on the roof that could affect the solar installation?
verdicts.designer_answer: details: Solar water heater will affect the solar installation.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7 and page 11: 'Supreme Solar' evacuated-tube solar water heater sits on the terrace inside the marked 'PV propose area'; a yellow water tank sits on the headroom; page 11 caption says the heater will be removed by the customer.
verdicts.rationale: The solar water heater the designer names is clearly visible inside the proposed PV area. Its removal is customer scope (Observation #4) and should be tracked before installation.

verdicts.question: What is the angle of the panels? (in degrees)
verdicts.photo_observation: No site photo of installed panels (new install). The 3D renders on pages 9-10 show a low-tilt elevated array; the visible tilt looks roughly 10-15 degrees.
verdicts.rationale: The design renders show a low tilt that fits 10 degrees. The exact angle can't be measured from a perspective render.

verdicts.question: On how many roofs at the site are we installing solar?
verdicts.photo_observation: Top view (page 8) and side views (page 9) show one six-panel array on a single terrace; the PV area marked on page 11 is one contiguous terrace zone.
verdicts.rationale: Single roof/array consistent across layout and site photo.

verdicts.question: What type of mounting structure is planned?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 10 render: a raised structure on four legs with base plates and a '2.0 m' dimension marked at the front edge; page 9 side views show the array raised above the parapet.
verdicts.rationale: The render explicitly shows an elevated structure with 2.0 m clearance. HDGI material can't be confirmed visually. Note: the 'Mounting Structure Type' field on page 2 says 'RCC Flat Roof' (roof type, not structure), which is a minor data-entry inconsistency.

verdicts.question: What is the orientation of the solar panels?
verdicts.photo_observation: Side view (1) on page 9: the compass S arrow points right and the array's lower edge is on the S side. In side view (2), the array dips toward the S label. Top view (page 8) has a N-up compass with the array at the south-west corner.
verdicts.rationale: The renders with compass roses show the panels tilted toward the south. There's no on-site compass photo.

verdicts.question: How can the roof be accessed?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 6: internal granite staircase with railing (about 0.5 m tread width annotated). Page 7/8: red-painted concrete steps going up onto the terrace. A ladder to the headroom top is also visible on page 7.
verdicts.rationale: Staircase access to the terrace is clearly shown.

verdicts.question: Is the building currently under construction?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 5-6, 12: fully plastered and painted exterior, finished jali panels, tiled canopies, installed windows, granite stairs and an occupied interior. No scaffolding or bare brick.
verdicts.rationale: Building is clearly finished and occupied.

verdicts.question: What is the height of the building and how many floors does it have?
verdicts.designer_answer: Height of the building is 14m; it has G+3 floors
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 5 front shows the ground-floor entrance gate plus about 2 visible upper storeys with jali balconies, with the top partly cut off by the sun. Page 6 side elevation shows about 3-4 window bands up to the terrace with a tiled canopy/headroom. Page 13 shows a sunken side passage (possible basement level).
verdicts.rationale: Floor count is ambiguous: the photos could show G+2+headroom or G+3, and a sunken/basement level may exist. Height can't be measured from the photos.

verdicts.question: Is the site photo matching with the building description?
verdicts.photo_observation: Building Exterior (page 5) and side elevation (page 6) show a multi-storey residential house with an RCC flat terrace, matching the residential sector and RCC flat roof description. The site address is a layout plot with open land around it.
verdicts.rationale: The photos are consistent with the residential RCC building described. The exact floor count is checked separately under roof Q13.

verdicts.question: Is there an overhead HT line passing within a 10-meter radius of the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 5 (both photos) and page 6 (bottom): several overhead conductors run very close to the building at upper-floor/terrace height, a few metres from the facade. A pole is visible at the left of page 6.
verdicts.rationale: Overhead lines are clearly within 10 m of the building. They look like LT distribution/service lines, but the voltage class can't be confirmed from the photos. Their closeness also matters for the exterior rope-lifting route.

verdicts.question: Can the delivery van/truck reach the material unloading point?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 5: a car parked directly at the front gate on a paved apron. Page 6 bottom: an unpaved but drivable road alongside the plot.
verdicts.rationale: Vehicle access right up to the gate is shown.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstacles at the site that could hinder material lifting?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 6: internal staircase annotated as 0.5 m wide (narrow), so large items are routed by an external lift along the side wall (blue line). That wall has a tree right next to it, dense shrubs at its base, and overhead wires near the roofline.
verdicts.rationale: A 0.5 m staircase is narrow for 2.28 m modules, and the external lift route has a tree, undergrowth and nearby overhead wires. This may count as a lifting obstacle, so please confirm.

verdicts.question: Where will the Inverter, DCDB, ACDB, Battery, etc. be located?
verdicts.designer_answer: Inverter, DCDB, ACDB, Battery is located near the top terrace.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 11 bottom (Cable Routing): a roofed alcove on the terrace beside the headroom, with 'Inverter and other components' and 'Battery' markers on its walls, an existing battery/UPS on the floor and a 'UPS point' marked.
verdicts.rationale: Equipment location on the terrace is clearly identified in the photo.

verdicts.question: Is a canopy required for protecting the Inverters/ACDB/DCDB?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 11 bottom: the equipment alcove has a concrete slab roof overhead and walls on three sides.
verdicts.rationale: The location is already sheltered by the RCC slab, so no canopy is needed.

verdicts.question: Did you discuss the location of the earth pits with the customer?
verdicts.designer_answer: Location of the earth pits are in the basement area.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 13: a narrow paved side passage below plinth level between the building wall and the compound wall, with LA Pit, DC Earth Pit and AC Earth Pit markers. Page 12 bottom: earthing/LA conductor drops marked down the side facade.
verdicts.rationale: The earth pit locations are marked in a lower-level side passage, consistent with 'basement area'. The passage is paved with concrete, so the floor will need breaking/coring.

verdicts.question: Where is the Internet Router located?
verdicts.photo_observation: No router photo in the report. The Observations section lists 'Wi-Fi is under customer scope'.
verdicts.rationale: No photo shows the router. The answer matches the observations text but can't be checked visually.

verdicts.question: Did you pin the site location in your WhatsApp when you were at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Not something a photo can show. The report includes GPS coordinates (13.0780, 77.7073) and a Google Maps link on page 1.

verdicts.question: What type of energy meter is currently installed?
verdicts.designer_answer: Phase: Three Phase, Type: Digital, If 3-phase: LT w/o CT (5 - 34.999)
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7 Meter Box (zoomed): Landis+Gyr E250 with LCD display, label reads '3 PHASE 4 WIRE ENERGY METER, 3x240/415V 5-30A', BESCOM property. Whole-current terminal block with direct cable entry (no CTs), and three fuse carriers below.
verdicts.rationale: The meter label confirms a three-phase digital whole-current (5-30 A, no CT) meter.

verdicts.question: Is the Meter cubicle photo matching with the previous answer?
verdicts.photo_observation: Meter cubicle photos on page 7 and page 12 show the same 3-phase digital Landis+Gyr meter with three cut-outs in a grey MS enclosure.
verdicts.rationale: The cubicle photo matches the three-phase digital whole-current answer.

verdicts.question: Has the termination point in the Main meter panel been identified?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 12 Equipment Location: the main meter is highlighted in red with a purple line from a proposed 'Solar meter' position on the wall to its left into the main meter enclosure.
verdicts.rationale: The termination path into the main meter panel is marked. The exact terminal/breaker isn't called out.

verdicts.question: Is the Termination Point easily visible or sealed?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7 zoom: terminals are visible through a transparent terminal cover, but a blue utility (BESCOM) seal is fitted on the right side of the meter/terminal cover. The adjacent main switch panel on page 12 is open and accessible.
verdicts.rationale: The terminals can be seen but the meter terminal cover carries a utility seal, so 'Visible' vs 'Sealed' is ambiguous. Confirm whether termination is at the sealed meter or at the open main switch panel.

verdicts.question: Is a Lightning Arrestor (LA) already available at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: None of the terrace/headroom photos (pages 7, 8, 11) show a lightning arrestor rod or down conductor. The new LA pit and LA cable are planned (pages 12-13).
verdicts.rationale: No existing LA is visible, and a new LA pit is planned, which fits 'No'. Not every part of the roof is photographed.

verdicts.question: In Main meter panel, is empty space available for solar meter?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7/12: the main meter compartment is fully occupied by the existing meter and three cut-outs. The solar meter is proposed outside the panel on the wall to its left (page 12).
verdicts.rationale: The full enclosure and the external solar meter placement support 'No'.

verdicts.question: Is there space available to dig DC, AC and LA earth pits?

verdicts.question: What type of Earthing chamber needs to be installed at site? Is it Cement chamber or PVC chamber?

verdicts.question: In case of elevated structures, is an LA extension provided at the far end?

verdicts.rationale: The LA extension at the far end isn't drawn in the structure renders. Only the LA pit and down-conductor are shown.

verdicts.question: In case of elevated structures, is it with or without grouting?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 10 render: structure legs end in base plates sitting on the slab. No grouting pedestals or anchors are detailed.
verdicts.rationale: The foundation type (grouted vs anchored) can't be told from the render.

verdicts.question: Are there any challenges with respect to Installation and Maintenance activities?
verdicts.photo_observation: Photos show the existing solar water heater inside the PV area and an existing battery/UPS in the equipment alcove, both to be removed by the customer (pages 11, 13). The elevated structure is 2 m high, the staircase is 0.5 m wide, and large items need an external lift.
verdicts.rationale: There are several practical constraints (customer removals, narrow staircase, external lifting, 2 m elevated structure) that could be seen as challenges. Not a clear contradiction, but please confirm.

verdicts.question: Are there any safety risks associated with accessing the roof for installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: Roof access is by a railed internal staircase and the terrace has parapets (pages 6-8). However, overhead conductors pass close to the upper floors (page 5) along the exterior material-lift route, and a ladder is used for the headroom/water tank.
verdicts.rationale: Normal roof access looks safe. Overhead lines near the external lifting route are a possible safety risk to confirm.

verdicts.question: Is space present in rooftop to store the panels?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 8 Material Storage: open terrace floor beside the stair with tall parapet/headroom walls that panels could lean against.
verdicts.rationale: There is wall space on the terrace for leaning six 2.28 m panels vertically.

verdicts.question: Is ventilation available in the battery location?

verdicts.question: Is there any shadow that affects the solar installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: Top view (page 8): the array is at the south-west corner, and the headroom with water tank and the solar water heater (to be removed) are to the north/north-east. The array is raised 2 m. Page 11 shows no tall structures to the south; nearby trees are below terrace height.
verdicts.rationale: The headroom is north of the array and the structure is elevated, so no meaningful shading is expected. This assumes the solar water heater is removed.

verdicts.question: Is there any trench work to be done to carry the AC cable to the meter location?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 12: the main meter panel is wall-mounted on the building, and the earthing/LA routing (page 12 bottom) runs down the facade. There's no route across open ground to a remote meter.
verdicts.rationale: The meter is on the building itself, so the cable can run down the wall without a trench.

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 11 top/bottom: red and green lines run from the PV area along the parapet, up the headroom wall and into the terrace alcove ('Inverter and other components'). Page 12 top: a purple line from 'Solar meter' into the main meter. Page 12 bottom / page 13: green and orange earthing/LA lines drop down the side facade to the pits. No photo shows the AC run from the terrace inverter/ACDB down the building to the ground-floor solar meter. Conduit/clipping isn't specified anywhere.
verdicts.rationale: The terrace segment (PV to inverter) and the meter segment (solar meter to main meter) are drawn, but the inverter/ACDB to solar meter AC run down the building is missing, leaving a gap in the documented route. Conduit or clipping details aren't shown.
